translations.text: And God said, “Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let there be a division between water and water.” And it was so.
And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of heaven to give light upon the earth and to divide the day from the night, and let them serve as signs and for seasons, days, and years.”
And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.
And God placed them in the expanse of heaven to give light upon the earth.
And God said, “Let the waters bring forth swarms of living creatures and winged birds above the earth along the expanse of heaven.” And it was so.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: four-footed animals, creeping creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.

And every plant of the field, before it existed upon the earth, and every grass of the field, before it had sprouted, for the Lord God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no human being to cultivate the earth.
And Adam named his wife Eve, because she is the mother of all the living.
And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of delight to cultivate the earth from which he had been taken.
But he did not look with favor upon Cain and his offerings, and Cain was deeply grieved, and his face fell downward.
And Seth had a son, and he named him Enosh. He hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God.
Adam lived two hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his own likeness and according to his own image, and he named him Seth.
And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
And Enoch was pleasing to God for two hundred years after he fathered Methuselah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And all the days that Methuselah lived were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.
And from the clean birds and from the birds that were not clean, and from the clean animals and from the animals that were not clean, and from all the creeping creatures that creep upon the earth.

They and every wild animal according to its kind, and all livestock according to their kinds, and every creeping creature that moves upon the earth according to their kinds, and every flying bird according to its kind.
And the water rose and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved upon the waters.

And the dove, finding no resting place for its feet, returned to him in the ark, because water still covered the whole surface of the earth. And he stretched out his hand and received it and brought it back to himself in the ark.
And he waited seven more days and again released the dove, and it no longer returned to him.
“Whoever sheds human blood, his blood shall be shed in return for that blood, for I made humankind in the image of God.
“But you, be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and multiply upon it.
“And behold, I establish my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,

“And with every living creature that is with you, among the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals of the earth that are with you, and among all that came out of the ark and all the animals of the earth.”
And the sons of Javan were Elishah and Tarshish, the Kittites and the Rhodians.
And the whole earth had one language and one form of speech for everyone.
And the Lord said, “Look, they are one people, and they all have one language, and they have begun to do this. Now nothing they wish to do will be beyond their reach.”
“Come, let us go down and confuse their languages there, so that each one will not understand the speech of his neighbor.”
And after fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived five hundred years and had sons and daughters, and he died.
And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there as a foreigner, because the famine had become severe in the land.
And Lot, who had gone with Abram, had cattle, sheep, and other livestock.
And the land was not sufficient for them to live together, because their possessions were great, and they could not live together.
They also took Lot, Abram’s nephew, and his possessions, and went away, for he had been living in Sodom.
And immediately the voice of God came to him and said, “This man will not be your heir, but the one who comes from you will be your heir.”
And near sunset a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and suddenly a terror of darkness came upon him.
“And he will be a wild man; his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him, and he will live opposite all his brothers.”
And Hagar bore Abram a son, and he named his son, whom Hagar bore to him, Ishmael.
And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
And Abraham said to God, “May this Ishmael live before you!”
On that very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.
Sarah denied it and said, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. And he said, “No, you did laugh.”
And the men rose from there and looked toward the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, and Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
“If the fifty righteous people fall short by five, will you destroy the whole city because of those five?” And he said, “I will not destroy it if forty-five are found there.”
And he said, “Since I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, what if twenty are found there?” And he said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty.”

And they were distressed, and the angels took him by the hand, and his wife by the hand, and his two daughters by the hand, because the Lord had mercy on him. They brought him out and placed him outside the city.
“And now hurry to escape there, because I cannot do anything until you arrive there.” For this reason he called the name of that city Zoar.
And the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no one on earth to come in to us as is the custom throughout the earth.”
And that night also they gave their father wine to drink, and the younger daughter went in and lay with her father. He did not know when she lay down or when she rose.
And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day when his son Isaac was weaned.
After these things, God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey, while the boy and I go over there, worship, and return to you.”
Isaac said to Abraham his father, “Father!” And he said, “What is it, my son?” And he said, “Here is the fire, and here is the wood, but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
Sarah died in the city of Kiriath-arba, in the valley—that is, Hebron—in the land of the Canaanites. Abraham came to lament Sarah and mourn her.

“The Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth, who took me from my father’s house and from the land where I was born, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to your descendants,’ will send his angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife from there for my son Isaac.”

“Let the maiden to whom I say, ‘Lower your jar so that I may drink,’ and who says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels until they have finished drinking,’ be the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham.”
When all the camels had finished drinking, the man took gold earrings, each weighing one daric, and two bracelets for her hands, weighing ten darics together.
She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
“But you shall go to my father’s house and to my family, and take a wife from there for my son.”

He said to me, “The Lord my God, in whose presence I have been pleasing, will send his angel with you and make your journey successful. You will take a wife for my son from my family and from my father’s house.”
I rejoiced and worshiped the Lord, and blessed the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who successfully guided me here on the path of truth to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
The servant brought out gold objects, silver objects, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave gifts to her brothers and her mother.
These are the years of Abraham’s life that he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years.
The field and the cave were those that Abraham acquired from the sons of Heth. There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.
These are the descendants of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s maidservant, bore to Abraham.
Isaac lived among the people of Gerar.

Isaac again dug the wells of water that the servants of his father Abraham had dug and that the Philistines had stopped up after the death of his father Abraham. He gave them the same names that Abraham his father had given them.
He went and brought them to his mother, and she prepared savory food just as his father liked.
Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Get up, sit, and eat some of my game, so that your soul may bless me.”
He did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of his brother Esau, and he blessed him.
He said, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”
Jacob left Beersheba and went to Haran.
“and brings me back safely to my father’s house, then the Lord will be my God.”
While he was speaking with them, Rachel, Laban’s daughter, came with her father’s sheep, for she tended her father’s sheep.
Laban said to him, “You are of my bones and of my flesh.” And he stayed with him for a month.
When Rachel saw that she had borne Jacob no children, she became jealous of her sister and said to Jacob, “Give me children, or I will die.”
Rachel said, “God has helped me, for I wrestled with my sister and prevailed.” And she named him Naphtali.
Laban said, “Tell me what wages you want from me, and I will pay them.”
The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks bore young that were gray-speckled, spotted, and mottled.
He said to them, “I see that your father’s face is not toward me as it was yesterday and the day before, but the God of my father has been with me.”
“All the wealth and glory that God has taken from our father shall belong to us and our children. Now do whatever God has told you.”
Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and called his brothers to eat bread. They ate and drank and spent the night there on the mountain.
He took them across the ravine, along with everything he owned.
Esau ran to meet him, embraced him and kissed him, fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they both wept.
Shechem, the son of Hamor the Horite, who was the ruler of the land, saw her, took her, lay with her, and violated her.
“Will not their possessions, their livestock, and their four-footed animals become ours? Only let us become like them in this, and they will live among us.”
He built an altar there and named the place Bethel, because God had appeared to him there when he was fleeing from his brother Esau.

These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, and chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
Joseph had a dream and told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more.
Israel said to Joseph, “Are not your brothers grazing the flocks at Shechem? Come, I will send you to them.” He said to him, “Here I am.”
“Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let us not stain our hands with him, for he is our brother and our own flesh.” And his brothers listened to him.
Midianite merchants passed by, and they pulled Joseph up out of the pit and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty coins. And they brought Joseph down to Egypt.
Onan knew that the offspring would not be his. Whenever he went in to his brother’s wife, he spilled his seed on the ground so as not to give his brother offspring.
Judah said, “Let her keep those things, lest we become a laughingstock. I sent this young goat, but you did not find her.”
After three months, Judah was told, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and now she is pregnant through her prostitution.” Judah said, “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”
As they were taking her away, she sent word to her father-in-law, saying, “I am pregnant by the man to whom these pledges belong.” And she said, “Recognize whose ring, necklace, and staff these are.”
When he drew his hand back, his brother immediately came out. She said, “Why has a barrier been broken through because of you?” And she named him Perez.
One such day, Joseph went into the house to do his work, and none of the household was inside.
She spoke to him in these words, saying, “The Hebrew slave whom you brought to us came in to me to make sport of me, and said to me, ‘Lie with me.’
“But when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me and fled outside.”
The captain of the guard entrusted them to Joseph, and he attended to them. They remained in that prison for some time.
In three more days Pharaoh will remember your office and restore you to your position as cupbearer. You will place Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you did formerly when you were his cupbearer.
Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “Without God there can be no answer concerning Pharaoh’s deliverance.”
The seven thin and ugly heifers ate the first seven heifers, which were beautiful and choice.
Joseph had two sons before the seven years of famine came. Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore them to him.
“And by this prove yourselves: as surely as Pharaoh lives, you will not leave here unless your youngest brother comes here.”
He put them in prison for three days.
Joseph withdrew from them and wept. Then he returned to them and spoke with them. He took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.

He said, “My son will not go down with you, because his brother has died, and he alone is left. If he should fall ill on the journey you are taking, you will bring my old age down to the realm of the dead in sorrow.”
“But if you do not send our brother with us, we will not go, because the man told us, ‘You must not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.’”
Israel said, “Why have you brought trouble upon me by telling the man that you have a brother?”
The man did as Joseph had said and brought the men into Joseph’s house.
They received their portions from him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of theirs. They drank and became drunk with him.
“Put my silver cup in the youngest one’s sack, along with the money for his grain.” And it was done according to Joseph’s word, just as he had said.
When he found them, he spoke these words.
Judah approached him and said, “Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word before you. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are next to Pharaoh.”
“We said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he leaves his father, he will die.’”
“Your servant, our father, said to us, ‘You yourselves know that my wife bore me two sons.’”
“‘One went away from me, and you said that he had been devoured by a wild beast. I have not seen him again to this day.’”
“So it was not you who sent me here, but God. He made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his household, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.”
“Now hurry and go up to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt. Come down to me now, and do not delay.’”
He gave each of them two robes, and to Benjamin he gave three hundred gold coins and five changes of robes.
The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
The sons of Gad were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
These were the children of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. The sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel.
And the sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.

And Joseph’s sons born in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore him, were Manasseh and Ephraim. And Manasseh’s son, whom the Syrian concubine bore him, was Machir, and Machir fathered Gilead. And the sons of Ephraim, Manasseh’s brother, were Shuthelah and Tahan, and Shuthelah’s son was Edem.
And Benjamin’s sons were Bela, Becher, and Ashbel. And Bela’s sons were Gera, Naaman, Anachis, Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Gera fathered Ard.

And they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in this land, because there was no pasture for your servants’ flocks, for the famine grew severe in the land of Canaan. So now let your servants settle in the land of Goshen.”
And Joseph supplied his father, his brothers, and his father’s entire household with grain, according to the number of mouths.
Joseph said to them, “Bring your livestock, and I will give you bread in exchange for your livestock, if your silver has run out.”

And they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. And he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock during that year.
“But I will lie down with my fathers, and let them carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their tomb.” And he said, “I will do as you say.”
Jacob was informed, and they said, “Look, your son Joseph is coming to you.” And Israel gathered his strength and sat up in bed.
Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore, and he shall be a harbor for ships, and shall extend as far as Sidon.
Joseph is a flourishing son, a flourishing, envied son. My young son, turn to me.

The blessings of your father and your mother, which surpassed the blessings of the everlasting mountains and the blessings of the eternal hills, shall be upon Joseph’s head and upon the head of the brothers whom he led.
Forty days were completed for him, for that was how the days for burial were counted, and Egypt mourned for him for seventy days.
And Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid, for I too belong to God.”
